english: Consider the curve $C$ given by $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}-3t$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. The tangent to $C$ at the point with parameter $t=1$ meets $C$ again at the point $Q$. If the normal to $C$ at $Q$ meets the $x$-axis at $(\alpha,0)$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: वक्र $C$ पर विचार कीजिए जो $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}-3t$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$ द्वारा दिया गया है। प्राचल $t=1$ वाले बिन्दु पर $C$ की स्पर्श रेखा $C$ को पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। यदि $Q$ पर $C$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष को $(\alpha,0)$ पर मिलता है, तो $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3t^{2}-3}{2t}$; at $t=1$ the slope is $0$, point $(1,-2)$, tangent $y=-2$.
Slope at $t=-2$: $\dfrac{12-3}{-4}=-\dfrac94$, so the normal has slope $\dfrac49$: $y+2=\dfrac49(x-4)$
solution_full: At $t=1$: point $(1,-2)$, slope $0$, so the tangent is the horizontal line $y=-2$.
Points of $C$ on $y=-2$: $t^{3}-3t+2=0\Rightarrow (t-1)^{2}(t+2)=0$. The double root $t=1$ is the point of contact, so the tangent meets $C$ again only at $t=-2$, i.e. $Q=(4,-2)$.
At $t=-2$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3(4-1)}{-4}=-\dfrac94$, so the slope of the normal at $Q$ is $\dfrac49$.
originality_note: New: tangent at one parameter re-meeting a cubic parametric curve, then the normal at the second point (way 1, one step of a tangent chain). Closest known: semicubical parabola x = t^2, y = t^3 where the tangent at t meets again at -t/2. Different because: the curve x = t^2, y = t^3 - 3t is not a listed skeleton, and the re-meeting point comes from a factorisation (t-1)^2(t+2).
blueprint_concepts: Tangent and normal for a parametrically defined curve

concept_use.Tangent and normal for a parametrically: dy/dx = (3t^2-3)/(2t) gives the tangent at t = 1 and the normal at t = -2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (positive decimal); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked the tangent at t = 1 meets the curve again at exactly one point. No change.
key_step: Factor t^3 - 3t + 2 = (t-1)^2(t+2) to find Q, then write the normal at Q.
justification: Routine chain of parametric slope, re-intersection by factorisation and normal: three standard steps with no insight, L2 like 2026-P2-Q2; easier than the L3 derivative anchor 2025-P2-Q14.
